newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up under some gas pressure.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up under some gas pressure.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended higher Wednesday under some pressure from higher spot natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Physical gas prices climbed Wednesday on forecasts of below-normal weather in the U.S. Mid-West and a pipeline leak in Louisiana.

Although higher gas prices were seen putting some pressure on electricity, brokers cautioned that power futures volumes were thin enough that the upward move may not have been based on concrete market fundamentals.
"This market is thin enough that for a couple of parties with a strong interest in moving the market, it wouldn't take too much," one futures broker said.

November California Oregon Border (COB) settled 52 cents higher at $17.92 after trade as low as $17.40 per megawatt hour (MWh), while December finished up 23 cents at $18.98 after trading as low as $18.70.
Remaining COB deferreds ended steady to up to 15 cents higher.
November Palo Verde (PV) ended up 62 cents at $17.47 per MWh after trade as high as $17.75, while December PV closed up 40 cents at $17.80 after trade as high as $17.95 per MWh.
January PV settled up 25 cents, whle remaining PV deferreds settled steady to 10 cents lower.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 138 COB and 255 PV contracts traded Wednesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
